raw_segments.text: The next day was as fine as its predecessor. It was devoted by the party to an excursion
to some site in the neighborhood. They set out early in the forenoon, some on horseback,
the rest in carriages. I witnessed both the departure and the return.
Miss Ingram, as before, was the only lady equestrian. And as before, Mr. Rochester galloped
at her side. The two rode a little apart from the rest. I pointed out this circumstance
to Mrs. Fairfax, who was standing at the window with me.
